text.title: Freelancer Inbound Reply Template Core Rules
text.summary: Seven rules constraining the four-line first-touch reply: exactly one qualifier, an acknowledgement that quotes the sender, a trust signal that resolves to something checkable, a next step with a slot in it, no price before scope, and the qualifier placed where the preview shows it.

rule.statement: qualifier_line asks for exactly one of scope, budget or deadline, and the whole reply contains at most one question mark. Two asks in the first reply is a rejection, however short they are.
rule.rationale: A second question usually needs information the sender does not have in front of them, so the reply stops being answerable in the same sitting and becomes a small task to schedule. Deferred replies to a cold-ish thread mostly never come back, and the freelancer reads the silence as disinterest rather than as friction they added.

rule.statement: acknowledge_line MUST contain at least one concrete noun lifted from sender_excerpt — the product, the stack, the company, the named deadline. An opener that would render identically for any inbound ("Thanks for reaching out, sounds interesting!") fails this check.
rule.rationale: The sender is triaging several near-identical replies and the only cheap discriminator available to them is whether the message could have been sent before reading theirs. A reply with no borrowed token is filed as an auto-response, and the thread is judged before its content is read.

rule.statement: trust_signal MUST be one of: a URL to work the sender can open, a named prior client the operator has permission to name, or a number with unit and period ("cut checkout p95 from 900 ms to 210 ms over six weeks"). Years of experience, stack lists and self-description do not satisfy it.

rationale.source: Internal — inbound reply audits across solo engagements

rule.rationale: Every competing reply in that inbox contains the unverifiable version, so it carries no discriminating information and is skimmed past. A resolvable artefact is the only clause the sender can act on without a call, which is what lets them advance the thread without spending a meeting first.

rule.statement: next_step proposes exactly one action, and it carries either two named slots with a stated timezone or one specific async question. "Let me know what works for you" and a bare booking link with no proposed time are rejected.

rationale.source: Fisher & Ury, Getting to Yes — making a yesable proposition

rule.rationale: An open-ended proposal hands the sender the scheduling work, so the cheapest reply becomes no reply. Two concrete slots reduce the response to picking one, which is the smallest decision that still advances the thread.

rule.statement: When qualifier_line asks about scope, the reply MUST NOT contain a day rate, hourly rate, project total or range. A price may appear only in a reply whose qualifier is budget, and then only as a range tied to a named comparable engagement.
rule.rationale: A number quoted before the work is defined is anchored to the smallest reading of the brief. Every scope detail discovered afterwards is then experienced by the client as a price increase from your first figure rather than as a line item, and the negotiation starts from your number instead of from the work.

rule.statement: In the rendered message, qualifier_line appears within the first two lines — after the acknowledgement and before the trust signal. Background about the operator MUST NOT precede it. Total reply length stays at or under about 120 words.

rationale.source: LinkedIn and mobile mail client preview truncation

rule.rationale: The recipient decides whether to open on a two-line preview in a notification list. A qualifier buried below a paragraph of background is invisible at that moment, so the message is judged on the background instead — and the one question that would have moved the deal never gets read on the phone where inbound is actually triaged.

rule.statement: Skip when the sender is an existing client (reply in the project channel instead) or when the inbound is a mass recruiter message naming a stack the operator does not work in. Emit a structured skip rather than a filled artefact.
rule.rationale: A qualifier sent to an existing client re-opens a scope conversation that already has a contract, and a warm-lead template used on a mass message spends a real trust signal on a recipient who is not reading the reply.
